You spent three and a half days last year, just sitting in traffic.
That's eighty-four hours of KL rush hour. Why? Because in Malaysia, driving is the easy option, almost by design.
Over forty million vehicles are registered here. That's more vehicles than Malaysians.
Petrol is subsidised. Car loans stretch up to nine years. And national cars keep prices low.
Meanwhile, only about one in five trips in the Klang Valley is by public transport. The target was forty percent.
Because the train often doesn't reach your door. You still need a car, or a Grab, just to get to the station.
Across the Causeway, just the right to own a car costs about a hundred and thirty thousand Singapore dollars.
And building more roads? Economists call it induced demand. New highway, more drivers, same jam.
